request.spec:
Selected claims can be settled together with one button, each in list order (people as added,
newest claim first within a person) by exactly the rules of settling one claim, by the signed-in
user: a claim that goes to PENDING counts as settled by the button, a claim that cannot be settled
is left as it is. Show how many were settled and how many were refused. Each claim that went
through writes its own lines as a single settle would.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be settled together with one button, each in list order (people as added,
newest claim first within a person) by exactly the rules of settling one claim, by the signed-in
user: a claim that goes to PENDING counts as settled by the button, a claim that cannot be settled
is left as it is. Show how many were settled and how many were refused. Each claim that went
through writes its own lines as a single settle would.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added a "Settle selected claims" button, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:**
- The button is in the new `src/main/frontend/features/claims/BulkSettle.tsx`. It's a copy of the existing "Open selected claims" (`BulkOpen.tsx`) with the action changed to settle. It sits on the home screen just below that button, set up in `features/claims/home.slot.tsx`.
- It goes through the ticked claims in list order (people in the order they were added, newest claim first within each person). Each one uses the same settle request as the claim's own Settle button, as the signed-in user.
- All the settle rules therefore apply exactly as for a single claim, and so do the audit lines: each claim that goes through writes its own `CLAIM_SETTLED` or `CLAIM_PENDING` line. A claim that goes to PENDING counts as settled.
- A claim the server refuses is left as it is and counted as refused. Examples are a draft, a claim in a closed period, or one opened by the same user. A ticked claim that is no longer on the sheet also counts as refused.
- Once it finishes, it shows "Settled N, refused M" (`bulk-settled`, `bulk-settle-refused`). It also clears the ticks and reloads the claims. The old counts disappear while it runs.

There were no server or data changes, because the existing settle endpoint already applies every rule.
